related_compound: chloroquine (the molecule actually tested in the anchor study; HCQ preferred clinically for wider safety margin)

approval.note: Both approved (antimalarial/rheumatic indications). Lysosomal autophagy inhibition is off-label.

claims.text: Direct aneuploidy-selective evidence: a phenotypic screen identified chloroquine - alongside AICAR and 17-AAG - as selectively antiproliferative to aneuploid versus euploid cells; autophagy inhibition is proposed to exploit the proteotoxic/metabolic stress state that aneuploid cells depend on.

Autophagy inhibition is an active cancer-therapy strategy: chloroquine-class agents sensitise tumour cells to cytotoxic and antiangiogenic therapy, and combined MAPK + autophagy blockade is under clinical translation in RAS-mutant cancers - supporting plausibility of the autophagy-dependence angle in aneuploid clones.

Disease link: MVA1 mosaicism means a lifelong stream of new aneuploid cells; a drug class that preferentially impairs aneuploid-cell proliferation could, in principle, trim the aneuploid compartment that seeds the cancer-predisposition phenotype. This is the Axis-C interception hypothesis - plausible, untested in MVA.

Counter-considerations: (i) the selective-kill data are cell-line/short-term; chronic systemic autophagy inhibition affects all tissues including those needing autophagy for quality control in a checkpoint-defective child; (ii) aneuploid cancer cells show complex, time-dependent responses to checkpoint/stress perturbation - not simple vulnerability; (iii) no study has tested CQ/HCQ in a BubR1/MVA model.

pediatric.label_source: openFDA drug/label set_id 04139607-f7c0-4fe1-a210-ffa5af347d56 (effective 2025-10-09); hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets
pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: Established in pediatric patients only for malaria treatment and prophylaxis, and only >=31 kg because tablets cannot be divided; NOT established for RA/discoid lupus/SLE in children (quoted label fact). Chloroquine label (set_id 06c69e2b-211b-4746-9f3a-f86d36520570) provides weight-based pediatric malaria dosing.
pediatric.label_pediatric_dosing_fact: Malaria prophylaxis >=31 kg: 6.5 mg/kg up to 400 mg weekly (quoted label fact, not advice). No pediatric dosing exists for any chronic indication.
key_risks: Retinal toxicity: label warns of irreversible retinal damage related to CUMULATIVE dose and duration, recommending baseline and ongoing retinal exams - the dominant concern for any chronic chemopreventive use in a young child.

Cardiomyopathy and ventricular arrhythmias incl. QT prolongation (fatal cases reported); serious skin reactions (SJS/TEN/DRESS); hematologic toxicity (myelosuppression); renal toxicity/phospholipidosis - relevant given nephrocalcinosis phenotype.
Chronic daily dosing for interception would exceed the cumulative exposure pattern the retinal-toxicity warning is anchored to; any use would need ophthalmologic surveillance from baseline.

celegans.expected: uncertain - autophagy inhibition may stress checkpoint-defective embryos either direction; informative either way

fibroblasts.assay: HCQ/CQ exposure on MVA patient fibroblasts (mosaic culture = internal euploid control)
fibroblasts.readout: differential viability of aneuploid vs euploid cells (FISH + live imaging or scDNA-seq after exposure), autophagic flux (LC3-II), micronuclei
fibroblasts.expected: selective reduction of aneuploid-cell fraction = the direct Axis-C test, uniquely possible in mosaic patient cells

verdict_reason: The only candidate with direct aneuploidy-selective antiproliferative evidence in the founding screen (PMID:21315436), and the only Axis-C drug whose target biology is exactly 'preferentially eliminate aneuploid cells'. The mosaic nature of patient fibroblasts makes the decisive experiment - selective depletion of aneuploid cells in the child's own cell model - directly testable with an internal euploid control. Kept out of the top tier by (i) selectivity shown for chloroquine in short-term cell assays, not validated in vivo or in MVA; (ii) irreversible retinal toxicity with cumulative exposure in a child who would need years of treatment; (iii) autophagy's double-edged role in a checkpoint-defective organism.
